# Conclusion

In this prospective, multicentre observational study across
`r n_center["final"]` hospitals in Germany and Austria,
passive CONTRAfluran canisters recaptured `r round(recovery_pct_final, 1)`%
of the sevoflurane attributable to the `r n_agcs["final"]` analysed canisters
under routine clinical conditions.
This finding is consistent with previous single-centre evidence
and extends it by demonstrating comparable recapture rates
across diverse clinical settings, anaesthesia workstations, and case mixes.

Exploratory penalised regression identified fresh gas flow
and the number of inhaled anaesthesia cases
as the main candidate predictors of per-canister recapture.
Water trap use was independently associated with higher recapture.
Stability selection corroborated only the dominant flow signal,
while the role of the remaining predictors remained uncertain at this sample size.
These findings indicate that the environmental return of vapour capture technology
is not uniform across operating rooms,
and that targeted deployment in settings with a high proportion of inhaled anaesthesia
may optimise capture efficiency at the system level.
